name: Belmond Palacio Nazarenas
positioning: Palacio Nazarenas, a Belmond hotel in a former palace and convent built upon ancient Inca ruins in Cusco
best_for: Travelers who want a historic convent-and-palace setting in Cusco
Guests who want oxygen-enriched suites and a spa while adjusting to altitude

facts.text: In 1644, Jesuits transformed the palace into a college for aristocratic children, and it later became a convent.
Original Inca stone walls give way to colonial-era frescoes and gilded 17th-century decor.
Chef Pia Leon leads the flagship restaurant Mauka, which draws on ingredients indigenous to Cusco and the Andes.
Senzo Bar serves small plates and Pisco cocktails.
The hotel serves afternoon tea with Andean botanicals.
The hotel has a heated outdoor swimming pool.
Hypnoze Spa offers treatments inspired by Inca and Andean culture.
The hotel is a short, cobblestoned walk up from Cusco's central plaza.
The hotel is a 20 minute drive from Alejandro Velasco Astete Airport.

highlights.text: The hotel is a former palace-turned-convent built upon ancient Inca ruins.
The spa is below ground, with glimpses of the Inca ruins unearthed during the restoration.
Suites have heated bathroom floors and pumped-in oxygen to help ease altitude issues.
Butler service is included for all rooms.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the high altitude location; the hotel offers oxygen-enriched accommodation.
Reaching the hotel from Cusco's central plaza involves a short, cobblestoned walk uphill.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Palacio Nazarenas, A Belmond Hotel, Cusco
